english.title: Fail to comply with a direction to investigate a railway accident - transport safety
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a

(A)_[manager of]_
(B)_[controller of]_
(C)_[person participating in the management of]_
(D)_[person participating in the control of]_

(E)_[railway property, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PROPERTY..),]_
(F)_[a part of railway property, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PROPERTY..),]_

(G)_[on which a railway accident or incident had taken place,]_
(H)_[which had been involved in a railway accident or incident,]_

failed to comply with a direction from the Chief Inspector of Rail Accidents to investigate the accident or incident under section 10 of the Railways and Transport Safety Act 2003
english.legislation: Contrary to section 10 of the Railways and Transport Safety Act 2003.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: A fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
